name: jumpnbump
title: Jump 'n Bump (Brainchild Design, 1998 — DOS/DJGPP)
fetch: git clone https://gitlab.com/LibreGames/jumpnbump.git corpus/jumpnbump && mkdir -p corpus/jumpnbump-dos && git -C corpus/jumpnbump archive $(git -C corpus/jumpnbump rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD) | tar -x -C corpus/jumpnbump-dos
_doc: THE ORIGINAL DOS SOURCE, and getting to it took some archaeology worth recording. The obvious trees are ports: the project's current head is SDL2, tag 1.51 is SDL 1.2, and even tag 0.72 -- which still carries dos/ -- CANNOT build for DOS, because its config.h opens with `#undef DOS` and every unit includes it through globals.h. A -DDOS on the command line is cancelled before it is read, so a DOS build there would mean EDITING the source. The one tree that is DOS without being selected is the CVS import at the repository's ROOT COMMIT (13 Feb 2002, 'Initial revision'): no config.h, no sdl/, no platform guard anywhere -- globals.h includes conio.h, dpmi.h, sys/nearptr.h, pc.h and dj.h unconditionally. Nothing to choose and nothing to patch. Brainchild's own tarball is not recoverable: brainchilddesign.com serves an empty page today, and the Wayback Machine has jnb-src.zip only as a 404 from 2021 -- the period download page offers the game and no source at all.
_units: modify/pack.c and modify/unpack.c are separate TOOLS that build the .dat file, not part of the game, and each has its own main().
_include: dj.h sits in dos/ and globals.h asks for it as <dj.h>, so dos/ is on the include path rather than the header being moved.
_sound: dj is a LIBRARY, and it ships here as dos/libdj.a with no source -- the binary names its own six units (dj.c mixer.c mod.c sb.c sb_dma.c sfx.c), a Sound Blaster DMA mixer with MOD playback. That is the Allegro and SEAL situation exactly (P1.7): the library is shimmed from its header, never compiled. dj.h declares 40 functions. NOTE that silence is not a compile-time option here -- NOSOUND exists in the later ports' config.h and is tested nowhere in the code -- but the API itself offers dj_set_nosound, which the program calls, so a silent build uses the library's own switch rather than an invented one.
_asm: dos/gfx.S is NASM syntax despite the .S extension ([GLOBAL _x], [SECTION .text]), and exports exactly TWO symbols: get_block and put_block, over ___djgpp_base_address. THIS TREE CARRIES NO C TWIN FOR EITHER -- gfx.c here has no #if 0 and never mentions them. (The disabled C versions belong to tag 0.72, the port's tree, and an earlier version of this note wrongly attributed them to the original.) So this is the first target in the corpus where assembly is NOT sidesteppable, which is a real data point for P5.2: that row measured an assembler buys ONE symbol corpus-wide, precisely because every other game ships C twins its own build can select. 215 non-empty lines and 24 distinct mnemonics -- mov/add/sub/cmp, five conditional jumps, shifts, imul, pusha/popa, and two out -- with no string ops, no floating point and no segmentation.
_videois_the_real_wall: NOT the assembly. gfx.c programs the VGA registers directly -- 0x3c4 (Sequencer) six times, 0x3ce (Graphics Controller) and 0x3c2 (Misc Output) -- and gfx.S selects a read plane through the Graphics Controller's Read Map Select with the page at a 32768-byte stride and 100 bytes per row. That is UNCHAINED PLANAR VGA, mode X, at 400x256: four planes behind 0xa0000, not the linear mode 13h every other DOS target here uses. src/env/allegro.js records that MAME needed no VGA register emulation because both its display paths end in _dosmemputl; this program is the first that does need one. It is roadmap P3.5, a DEVICE rather than a compiler feature, and the two assembly routines are the symptom rather than the wall.
_asmTranslate: The program's own assembly, translated by src/asm/ and bound as ordinary functions. Listed here rather than discovered: a .S file being present is not a reason to translate it, and every other target in the corpus ships a C twin its build selects instead. Checked against Unicorn on 400 random cases -- tools/gate-asm.mjs.
_env: vgaplanar is what makes this target paged: naming it says the 0xA0000 window is four planes rather than plain memory, and buildTarget turns compile.paged on for it. It is OPTIONAL even among DOS targets -- MAME writes the same VGA registers but leaves Chain-4 set, so its window stays linear and it names none of this, emitting exactly the JavaScript it always did.
